requirement:
A tracked read of an HC GitHub issue node records its identity and a fingerprint
of the supplied title, opening post, and status under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`.
Changing any of those supplied fields changes the fingerprint under the same
fingerprinting rules. The fingerprint excludes cache fetch time and TTL;
refetching otherwise unchanged issue contents does not change it.

The fingerprint describes the issue contents supplied under HC's
[redaction policy](../authoring.md#habeas-req-requirements.authoring.redaction),
including the text presented to an agent.
rationale:
Both reviewed tests are marked `{test}` for the subject. Together they cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.inputs`. I did not read the implementation.

**Identity and fingerprint recorded.**
- `src/sdk/issues.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tracked_issue_status_and_fingerprints_follow_refreshed_redacted_snapshots]` calls `validator.verify(OpenIssue(issue))`.
- It asserts that `first.dependencies()` equals exactly `[Dependency::Node(issue, supplied.fingerprint())]`. That is the node identity plus the fingerprint of the supplied contents, as `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` requires.
- The supplied text begins with the issue id, and it parses as JSON with `title`, `status` and `opening_post` fields. The test asserts the values of all three.

**Changing any supplied field changes the fingerprint.**
- The test loops over title, body and state, setting each in turn to a new value on the fake GitHub server.
- With the cache still fresh, `check_inputs(&previous)` stays true. After `expire`, it must return false, so the refetched contents fingerprint differently. This is asserted per field, with the field name as the message.
- It then re-verifies and asserts that the output matches the open or closed state.
- `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_detects_a_changed_reviewed_issue_body_while_repository_validation_stays_offline]` adds an end-to-end check for the body. A record's dependency fingerprint is taken from `node_content`. A changed body then produces the "reviewed issue changed" stale error, and an unchanged snapshot does not.

**Fetch time and TTL excluded; an unchanged refetch keeps the fingerprint.**
- After `expire(dir)`, the cache is stale and `check_inputs(&first)` refetches. The test asserts that `github.count()` goes from 1 to 2 and that the result is still true.
- A refetch with a new fetch time but the same contents therefore leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
- The changed-field step asserts the opposite while the cache is fresh, which is consistent with this.

**Redaction and presented text.**
- The body contains a `ghp_` token. The test asserts that the `opening_post` starts with `Wait until ready [REDACTED`.
- It also asserts that `supplied.format()`, the agent-presented text, does not contain the token.
- The fingerprint comes from the same redacted contents, which the dependency-equals-`supplied.fingerprint()` assertion ties together.

**Failed read.** After a 503 response and cache expiry, `node_content` returns an error containing "503". No observation is invented. This is context from `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and is not a separate obligation here.

I found no obligation without a test and no marking gap.

Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
